we have found a way to compute the changes to the MST of a directed graph over time, in time proportional to the number of changes, and have found a way, in time proportional, to the number of vertices and edges, to find the shortest bottleneck edge of the MST over time.

(1) we give a data structure to compute in linear time the MST over time for a class of parametric problems, and (2) for a class of problems that includes finding the shortest bottleneck edge, we give a data struc- ture that computes in linear time the bottleneck edge at all times.
In summary, our research is concerned with
parametric optimization problems, where the input is a graph and the objective function is a linear function of one parameter ("time").
parametric optimization problems that concern graphs with changing edge weights, and with a focus on the bottlenecks in the graph.
the shortest bottleneck edge in a parametric MST, which is the edge with the largest weight among all the edges of a given parametric MST.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MST of a graph with m edges can change at most m2/O(1) times over a linear change of edge weights, and that these changes can be enumerated or maintained in O(mn log n) total time.
the MST of a time-varying graph with m edges can be computed in O(mn2/3 polylog n) time, and can be maintained in O(n2 /3 polylog n) time per change.
for graphs of fixed size, the number of changes to the MST is O(n2/5), and the cost per change is Opoly(n).

we have developed a data structure for a graph with m edges and n vertices, with each edge weight a linear function of one or two parameters, to compute the shortest edge in the MST in constant time, with a cost of computing all changes to the edge weights of O(mn log n).

The main takeaway from our work is that
we can find the bottleneck edge in linear time (in mn).
the bottleneck edge of a MST (the one that is the tightest constraint on the MST weight) changes at most n-1 times per unit of time (or per unit of parameter).
